title: Add  UTF-8 debug checks and README notes
description:
Some older dissectors that predate Unicode and parse text protocols
are prone to generate invalid UTF-8 strings. This is a bug and can have
safety implications.

For example passing invalid UTF-8 to proto_tree_add_string() is a
common bug. There are safeguards in format_text() but this should
not be relied on as a general solution to the problem.

For one, as the name implies, it is only used with representation of a
field value, which is not the same as the value itself of an FT_STRING field.
Issue #18317 shows another reason why.

For now this compile flag only enables extra checks for string ftypes,
which covers a subset of proto.h APIs including
proto_tree_append_string(). Later is should be extended to other
interfaces.

This is also not expected to be disabled for release builds because
there are still many dissectors that do not correctly handle strings.
More work is needed to 1) identify them and 2) fix them.

Ping #18317

notes.body: /cc @johnthacker You have worked on this lately, let me know if you have comments or suggestions.

Related to #18317 I made some changes to do some safety checks / formatting to `proto_item_[append|prepend]_text()`, because some dissectors also pass bad UTF-8 strings to that, plus we generally want to format those strings to avoid internally displaying new lines, etc. Some dissectors already have a `format_text()` check, and it does waste time to run it through `format_text()` twice. In addition, `append_text()` is also used internally by some functions like `proto_item_add_bitmask_tree` and `proto_item_add_checksum`. In a few of that cases, it might be slightly faster to do something similar to make it optional (or have an internal "append but I know that this is a valid string because it's not coming from packet data") but since none of those have any effect when items aren't visible, it's probably not as bad as the `proto_tree_add_string_*` family.

Having that more aggressive check in there did find a few broken dissectors, at the cost of a number of fuzz test crashes. Maybe not something we want on in general, but I would like some way to have a little more than just a console warning when running fuzz testing.

I think that eventually all the various charset conversion functions should have a way of returning failure, so that dissectors (including those that call `tvb_get_string_enc()`) as well as `proto_tree_add_item()` can add expert info warnings for strings with bad encodings (or DISSECTOR_ASSERT() when running in more aggressive debug mode.)

I have some follow-up work planned for proto_item_append_text(). I don't think dissectors should be calling format_text(), for the most part. It is certainly a bug to pass text formatted for display to proto_item_add_string() and furthermore that function is heavily overused in the codebase.

I was thinking we could create a multibyte string encoding log domain and use that to enable more aggressive checks that could generate a backtrace.

Adding an expert info for encoding errors in sounds like a good idea.
I'm going ahead and merge this but I'd be interested in discussing the requirements for detecting encoding bugs with fuzz tests (and in general).

@geraldcombs  This assumes `build` is in the top level of the extracted source.  
It also exits on first error so needs something to process all files in case of multiple errors.  
Uncomment the `ln` and `mkdir` when moving to production.  

```
$ cat ./checksyms
#!/bin/sh

set -e

# ln -snf packaging/debian
# mkdir -p debian/tmp/DEBIAN


for i in wireshark wiretap wsutil; do
    echo ${i}
    NEW_VERSION=$(grep SOVERSION "$(grep -l lib${i} ./*/CMakeLists.txt)" | sed 's/.*SOVERSION \([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
    echo ${NEW_VERSION}
    dpkg-gensymbols -plib${i}${NEW_VERSION} -ebuild/run/lib${i}.so
done
```

changes_data.diff:
@@ -917,6 +917,32 @@ is also an essential component of a plugin system (libwireshark has plugins
 for taps, dissectors and an experimental interface to augment dissection with
 new extension languages).
 
+7.5 Unicode and string encoding best practices
+
+Wireshark strings are always encoded in UTF-8 internally, regardless of the platform
+where it is running. The C datatype used is "pointer to char" and this is assumed
+to point to a valid UTF-8 string. Sometimes older code uses char to point to opaque
+byte strings but this archaic usage should be avoided. A better data type
+for that is uint8_t.
+
+Every untrusted string needs to be validated for correct and error-free UTF-8
+encoding, or converted from the source encoding to UTF-8. This should be done
+at the periphery of the code. This means converting input during dissection or
+when reading input generally. To reiterate: all the Wireshark APIs expect to
+receive valid UTF-8 strings. These include proto_tree_add_string(),
+proto_item_append_text() and col_append_fstr() just to name a few.
+
+If a dissector uses standard API functions to handle strings, such as
+proto_tree_add_item() with an FT_STRING header field type, the API will
+transparently handle the conversion from the source encoding to UTF-8 and
+nothing else needs to be done to ensure valid string input.
+
+If your dissector does text manipulation, token parsing and such and generally
+extracts text strings from the TVBuff or tries to do line oriented input from
+TVBuffs it *must* make sure it passes only valid UTF-8 to libwireshark APIs.
+This should be done using tvb_get_string_enc() to extract a string from a TVbuff
+or get_utf_8_string() to validate a string after it has been constructed.
+
 8. Miscellaneous notes
 
 Each commit in your branch corresponds to a different VCSVERSION string
